Types

CarneError = object of CatchableError
JsArgKind = enum
  jakString,                ## string: strict JS string
  jakInt,                   ## int/int64: integral number (integral floats accepted)
  jakFloat,                 ## float: any number, ints widen
  jakBool,                  ## bool: strict boolean
  jakNimValue,              ## NimValue: eager snapshot of anything
  jakObject,                ## JSObjectRef: live object ref, arrays rejected
  jakRaw, ## JSValueRef: live ref, unchecked (overload dispatch,
           ## JS coercion passthrough)
  jakRest                    ## RestArgs: remaining raw refs (variadic tail, last only)
Declared registerFn parameter kinds. The macro maps the written type name to one of these at compile time; anything else is a build error. Valid type names: string, int, int64, float, bool, NimValue, JSObjectRef, JSValueRef, RestArgs. 
Module = ref object
  ctx*: JSContextRef
  ns*: JSObjectRef
A std module under construction: the JS context plus the namespace object that init returns for require("std/..."). 
NimValue = object
  case kind*: NimValueKind
  of nvkUndefined, nvkNull:
    nil
  of nvkBool:
    b*: bool
  of nvkInt:
    i*: int64
  of nvkFloat:
    f*: float
  of nvkString:
    s*: string
  of nvkArray:
    arr*: seq[NimValue]
  of nvkObject:
    obj*: OrderedTable[string, NimValue]
  of nvkFunction, nvkSymbol, nvkBigInt:
    raw*: JSValueRef
An eager snapshot of a JS value. Primitives, arrays and plain objects are deep-copied into Nim data; functions, symbols and bigints keep the borrowed raw ref, valid only for the duration of the callback that produced it (callers that retain must JSValueProtect separately, as std/http does for handlers). 
NimValueKind = enum
  nvkUndefined, nvkNull, nvkBool, nvkInt, nvkFloat, nvkString, nvkArray,
  nvkObject, nvkFunction, nvkSymbol, nvkBigInt
JS-facing value kinds. Numbers split: integral doubles become nvkInt (within ±2^53), the rest nvkFloat (incl. NaN/Infinity, which JSON cannot represent but JSC can). 
RestArgs = seq[JSValueRef]
Declared type of a variadic tail parameter. 
Runtime = ref object
  ctx*: JSContextRef
  argv*: seq[string]
  loop*: Loop
  pending*: int
  exitRequested*: bool
  exitCode*: int
  uncaught*: string
  instances*: Table[string, JSObjectRef]
  moduleStack*: seq[string]
  timerSeq*: int
  timers*: Table[int, TimerEntry]
  promiseSettled*: bool
  promiseRejected*: bool
  promiseText*: string
  source*: string
  sourceURL*: string
  baseDir*: string           ## Retained boot source so http workers can re-run the script.
Per-run shared state: JS context, argv, powpow loop, pending-work refcount, exit signalling, require cache, live timers. 
TimerEntry = object
  id*: TimerId
  fn*: JSObjectRef
  rest*: seq[JSValueRef]
  isInterval*: bool
One live JS timer: the powpow id, the protected JS callback, protected passthrough args, and whether it repeats.

Vars

colorTtyOverride: Option[bool] = none(bool)
CLI --isatty override for TTY detection, honored by useColor (cli.nim) and colorsOn (std/terminal). none = auto-detect from the actual stdout. Set once at startup, read-only afterwards.

Consts

maxDumpDepth = 64
Nesting cap for direct JS -> native-tree walkers (yaml, toml, xml, ...). Same contract as the snapshot cap: anything deeper throws instead of recursing forever on circular input.

proc buildCallbackFn(fname: string; ctxName: string; fnBody: NimNode;
                     params: seq[ParamSpec]): NimNode {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}

Builds the nested cdecl callback proc named fname. The header params generate the arity check plus one reader each (see parseHeader); the user body follows with the bindings in scope plus args, argumentCount and docBlock (the rendered JSDoc). Leading ## doc comments in the body are collected for error output: the JSDoc block prefixes type mismatches and is appended to arity and throwError messages:

module.registerFn readFile(path: string): ## fs.readFile(path) -> string ...

proc ensureLoop(rt: Runtime): Loop {....raises: [OSError], tags: [TimeEffect],
                                     forbids: [].}
Creates the run's powpow loop on first async need (timers, fetch, serve) and returns it. Pure-sync scripts never pay for the event backend (kqueue on macOS, epoll on Linux) + table preallocation. Every inc rt.pending site must go through here first, so pending > 0 implies a live loop.

proc readBytesParam(ctx: JSContextRef; v: JSValueRef;
                    fname, pname, docBlock: string; exception: ptr JSValueRef;
                    dst: var string): bool {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Reads a live value as bytes: JS strings contribute their UTF-8 bytes, Uint8Array/Uint8ClampedArray views and ArrayBuffers are copied out immediately (the JSC pointer is temporary and may not survive further JS calls). Anything else throws the JSDoc-first type mismatch, like the macro's checked params. Snapshots (NimValue) are deliberately avoided here: a Uint8Array would walk per byte. False + JS throw on failure.

proc sanitizeUTF8(s: string): string {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Copies s, replacing malformed UTF-8 with U+FFFD (WHATWG-style). JSC string creation fails on invalid input (nil JSString), which turns into dropped values or rejected fetches downstream — never pass wire bytes to newJSString unsanitized. Overlongs, surrogates and codepoints past U+10FFFF count as malformed, like WebKit.

    forbids: [].}
Converts a snapshot to the format funnel. Raises on kinds JSON cannot represent (undefined, functions, symbols, bigints, NaN/Infinity) — the same inputs jsToJson rejects today. 
proc toJSUint8Copy(ctx: JSContextRef; s: string; name: string;
                   exception: ptr JSValueRef): JSValueRef {....raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Copies s into a heap buffer owned by the Uint8Array (freed on GC). Fallback for files mmap cannot cover (empty, pipes, proc). nil + JS throw on failure. 
proc toJSUint8Mmap(ctx: JSContextRef; mem: pointer; byteLen: int; name: string;
                   exception: ptr JSValueRef): JSValueRef {....raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Wraps an mmap'd region as a Uint8Array, transferring ownership to JSC (munmap runs on GC). The caller must never touch mem or close the mapping afterwards, on success or failure (JSC runs the deallocator even when construction fails). nil + JS throw on failure. 
proc valueToString(ctx: JSContextRef; value: JSValueRef): string {....raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Converts a JS value via String(value). Empty string on failure.

Macros

macro init(def: untyped): untyped

Module initializer. Takes proc(<name>: Module) = ... and generates the install* entry point behind require("std/..."):

init proc(module: Module) = exportObject: module.property greeting = "hi" module.registerFn readFile(path: string): ...

module.registerFn defines the callback and attaches it to the namespace; module.property attaches a data value (string, int, float, bool, JsonNode). A ## doc comment on a member is collected for error output (see buildCallbackFn). Bare statements run as init-time setup code. Member declarations outside exportObject: are an error, as is anything but members inside it.

macro registerFn(ctx: untyped; header: untyped; fnBody: untyped): untyped

Defines a JSC callback with the standard JSObjectCallAsFunctionCallback shape. The header declares the parameter types (see parseHeader); arity and type checks are generated, so the body starts with the bindings in scope. The body also sees ctx (named after the passed context), function, thisObject, argumentCount, arguments, a pre-cast args and docBlock (the rendered JSDoc):

ctx.registerFn readFile(path: string): ## fs.readFile(path) -> string ...

Definition only; registration stays explicit, as before:

setProp(ctx, ns, "readFile", makeFunction(ctx, "readFile", readFile), addr ex)

Note: quote cannot express this (it is hygienic: injected bodies cannot see quote-introduced bindings), so the proc is built manually and body identifiers are substituted with gensyms. Nested routine definitions inside the body are left untouched.

Templates

template exportObject(body: untyped): untyped
Marker for member declarations inside init. Only init understands it; direct expansion is a compile error.
